title: Fandisk (figure_10): 24 of 112 motorcycle traces die at degenerate chart cells, leaving a T-mesh whose quantization ILP is infeasible
description:
Found while fixing PATCH-109. With the stalled-boundary handling from that ticket, ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_10/fandisk_in_tri.off no longer throws in the motorcycle stage, but its arrangement is poor and the pipeline then fails at quantization:

```
IllegalStateException: quantization ILP INFEASIBLE
  at QuantizedMeshGrid.build (QuantizedMeshGrid.java ~238)
```

QuantizedMeshGrid's doc says a consistent T-mesh always admits the all-ones solution, so INFEASIBLE means the T-mesh handed to it is inconsistent, not that the solver is at fault. The motorcycle log on fandisk shows why: `[motorcycle-diag] stalledBoundaryCrossings=24 stalledTerminations=24`. Twenty-four of the 112 traces hit a degenerate chart cell (a face whose chart image is a 1-ulp chord, so the trace ping-pongs between two faces with no forward exit) and PATCH-109 terminates them there after one boundary crossing. Each dead trace leaves a dangling arc end, which is why the arrangement reports 2465 patches of which only 607 are valid rectangles. PATCH-109 measured that letting a trace bounce more times (budget 8) made it worse (4699 cycles, 10374 law violations), so the chart degeneracy itself is the bug: fandisk's seamless map collapses some triangles to a line in the chart, and the walker cannot transport a level line through them.

Two candidate layers: (a) the seamless parametrization on fandisk produces near-zero-area chart triangles (fandisk has long thin CAD faces and sharp creases); check the injectivity metrics and whether these faces are the ones the injectivity loop leaves flipped or collapsed; (b) ChartWalker should handle a degenerate cell by transporting straight through it to the far edge instead of stalling. Whichever it is, the quantization stage should also report which constraint family is infeasible rather than a bare INFEASIBLE, so the next inconsistent T-mesh is diagnosable.
definition-of-done: 1. On fandisk the stalled-boundary counters are 0, or the remaining stalls are shown to be at genuinely degenerate source triangles that no chart can fix. 2. Fandisk's arrangement reports every cycle valid and 0 Def 3.1 violations, and the quantization ILP is feasible. 3. QuantizedMeshGrid names the violated constraint family and the arcs involved when the ILP is infeasible. 4. hand, rockerarm, botijo and elk keep their motorcycle statistics.
testing-plan: 1. In a worktree synced after PATCH-109 lands, load fandisk and reproduce. 2. Dump the 24 stalled traces: face ids, the chart triangle's area and edge lengths, and the seamless map's per-face distortion there. 3. Decide between fixing the chart (seamless) and the walker; implement; rerun. 4. Add the constraint-family report to the quantization failure. 5. Screenshots of the arrangement under tmp/; compare the other meshes' log lines.
unknowns: Does PATCH-90 (greedy basis-loop quantization replacing the ILP) change what happens with an inconsistent T-mesh, or does it need the same input fix?
changes-made: Reproduced on master 22c2d190: [seamless] Metrics flippedTriangleCount=0 meanDistortion=0.2524762729315883, injectivity '[injectivity] done violated=0 flippedTriangles=0', motorcycle stalledBoundaryCrossings=17 stalledTerminations=17, arrangement 2395 cycles / 617 valid rectangles / lawViolations=4695 / Def-3.1 violations=14, then 'quantization ILP INFEASIBLE' at separation round 29 (round 0 was OPTIMAL; the loop merged one singularity cluster every round and piled on cuts until they contradicted). No '[seamless] alignment guard' line on fandisk, so the PATCH-107 guard drops nothing here and is not implicated.

Diagnosis, unknown 1 answered: the chart cells are NOT degenerate. flippedTriangleCount counts uvSignedArea <= 0 and is 0, and the BCE13 loop ends violated=0. What is inexact is feature alignment: fandisk has 655 alignment rows (bolt 101, rockerarm 1, buddha 0) and the solve leaves a crease edge iso only to ~1e-13 (about 22 ulps of a chart magnitude ~25). A new ChartWalker.describeStalledFace dump shows every stall is a zero-advance exit on such a near-iso face, e.g. face 631 with c0.v=25.205228259708633 and c1.v=25.205228259708655 while the trace's level is exactly c0.v.

Root cause of the arrangement collapse: MotorcycleGraph.handleEdgeCrossing ignored EdgeHit.cornerLocalIndex, so a separatrix exiting exactly at a cone point crossed an incident edge and walked straight through the cone (124 of 208 corner exits). Past the cone it ran collinear with the separatrix that cone emits in the same direction, giving collinearMeetings=1768 and 2340 of 3571 nodes with an unorderable port fan. The ILP was a symptom: with 617/2395 valid rectangles there were only 63 consistency rows, the optimum zeroed 6708 of 7018 arcs, and the separation loop could never separate the merged cluster.

Fixes landed in this worktree. (1) MotorcycleGraph.handleEdgeCrossing routes a corner exit through ChartWalker.crossVertex, so a separatrix reaching a cone terminates there (LCBK19 Sec 3.1) instead of crossing an incident edge; the EdgeHit.cornerLocalIndex javadoc already promised this. (2) A collinear meeting ends both traces at the contact node (endCollinearOverlap): two separatrices on one iso line are the two halves of one curve, so anything past the contact would be traced twice. (3) FaceSegmentIndex's same-axis test compares iso levels with a 1e-11 tolerance instead of bit equality, because fandisk's near-duplicate separatrices arrive ~1e-13 apart and an exact test never sees the overlap. (4) A crossing on a face corner or on a mesh edge resolves to one T-mesh node (crossingNode/vertexNode/edgeNode), so one surface point never becomes two nodes, plus a post-simulation pass dropping meetings that repeat a node. (5) SnappingCarve.chartBarycentric pins a coordinate the inversion rounded past zero, and exitBarycentric handles a segment that ends inside its face. (6) PatchBoundaryBuilder counts a hop as at-a-singularity only for a critical or border vertex node.

Numbers on fandisk, before -> after: stalledBoundaryCrossings 17 -> 0; collinearMeetings 1768 -> 23 (all terminated); nodes with an ambiguous port fan 2340 of 3571 -> 20 of 769; arrangement 2395 cycles / 617 valid rectangles -> 697 cycles / 682 valid; hop-turn lawViolations 4695 -> 0; Def 3.1 rectangularity violations 14 -> 0; quantization ILP INFEASIBLE at separation round 29 -> OPTIMAL, converging in 2 separation rounds (objective 2365.796, zeroArcs 905/1496, violations 0). Seamless metrics unchanged (meanDistortion 0.2524762729315883), as PATCH-107 reported.

DoD item 3 done: QuantizedMeshGrid now re-solves with each constraint family dropped in turn when the ILP is infeasible and reports which family's removal restores feasibility, the separation round it failed on, and the per-family counts, instead of a bare state name. LayoutEmbedding.assertSubcomplex now names the contested copy edge and both arcs.

Regression caught and repaired during verification: two of my first-cut carve changes moved bolt and rockerarm. (a) chartBarycentric originally clamped any |coordinate| < 1e-13 to zero and renormalised, which flipped mintInside's dispatch from a face split to an edge split on points that were legitimately just inside; it now pins only a coordinate the inversion rounded BELOW zero, which cannot move a point that is genuinely inside. (b) A post-simulation pass that dropped meetings repeating a node also dropped the legitimate second entry a self-crossing records for its one node, costing bolt an arc and three patches; the pass is gone and SnappingCarve.exitBarycentric instead handles a segment that ends inside its face. After both repairs bolt is bit-identical to master again (arcs=1398 nodes=721 patches=679).

On fandisk it truncates 6 trails, arcsSharingANodePair drops to 0, the arrangement improves to 708 cycles / 706 valid rectangles with Def 3.1 violations 0, and the T-mesh now embeds ([embed] arcs=1479 copy V=11544 E=34626 F=23084) instead of failing assertSubcomplex.

Two more defects found and fixed after the partial-overlap rule. (1) endCollinearOverlap could kill a trace that had not yet laid any arc, when the collinear contact landed on that trace's own origin cone — two ports of one cone leaving along one line is not one separatrix riding on another, so an origin contact is no longer treated as an overlap, and finalizeOpenTraces no longer has to mint a dangling end in open space. (2) It also left the other trace off its own chain when the contact node was already its current node; it now always ends at the contact. Instrumented the corner-exit path as well: on fandisk cornerExits=22 with fanGaps=0 fanBoundaries=0, so master's crossVertex routing never gives up there.

Reworked on the coordinator's reading of the papers, which is the correct one. EGKT08 section 5: a particle stops 'when a particle meets a vertex that has previously been traversed by itself or another particle'. LCK21a section 3 relaxes that only for a crash where 'a regular valence 4 node is formed at the intersection', i.e. a transversal crossing. Driving along an existing trail forms no valence-4 node, so it must crash at trace time rather than be unpicked afterwards. Removed truncateTrailsOntoAnother and its dead-end side effects; endCollinearOverlap became crashOntoTrail, which stops the arriving trace always and the trail's owner only on a genuine head-on meeting (EGKT08's oppositely-travelling clause), instead of stopping both. FaceSegmentIndex no longer skips an origin contact for collinear chords, so a trace leaving its cone along an existing trail crashes there and lays no arc.

Evidence on the remaining fandisk overlap: arcsSharingANodePair equals sharedEdgeNodes exactly (11 = 11), so every surviving pair of arcs between one node pair sits on nodes that master's nodeAtChartPoint merged because two crossings landed on the same mesh EDGE from the two faces flanking it. The two traces never meet each other at all — each crosses a third trace at a point the other also crosses, within a rounding step, and the node merge then makes their chains coincide. A chord-level collinear test can never see this because FaceSegmentIndex is per face, which is why the crash rule was extended to compare trail directions in 3D at a node (PARALLEL_TRAIL_COS, 45 degrees); that took arcsSharingANodePair from 15 to 11, the arrangement to 728 cycles / 717 valid, and the double-claimed copy elements from 2 to 1.

hand's one behaviour change is now named exactly: trace 127 (from singularity vertex 3101) crashes head-on onto trace 114 (from vertex 2568) at node 40. That is a genuine head-on collinear meeting which master let both traces drive straight through, and which EGKT08's oppositely-travelling clause stops. hand still loads end to end at 1743/1743 valid rectangles with meanDistortion 0.16835723261213387; only the [embed] counts move (arcs 3537 -> 3562, copy V 13805 -> 13895, E 41409 -> 41679, F 27606 -> 27786). An earlier experiment that also surfaced collinear origin contacts in FaceSegmentIndex was reverted: fandisk reports ofThoseAtOrigin=0, so it bought nothing there while perturbing hand further.

Two candidate next steps: apply EGKT08's stop at the point nodeAtChartPoint REUSES an existing edge node (the arriving trace has by definition reached a point already on a trail, so the test needs no meeting between the pair), or revisit whether merging two crossings a rounding step apart on one mesh edge is right at all, since that merge is what makes two distinct curves share a node pair.

MC19 5.3 alignment block implemented in SeamlessProjector and it works: maxAlignmentResidual is now 0.0 (0 ulps) on every mesh, where it was 2.487e-13 on fandisk and 1.137e-13 on bolt. Three pieces: (a) computeAlignmentEdges reads SeamlessDofSystem.alignmentEdgeIsoAxis so the projector sees exactly the rows the dof system wrote, guard-dropped edges included; (b) isNode gains MC19's 'incident cut edge and incident align edge' clause so no aligned sector sits in a cut branch's interior where back-substitution would overwrite it; (c) the 1_k alignment block is eliminated by identifying columns rather than by adding rows - every alignment row is x_p|k - x_q|k = 0 with unit coefficients, so its transitive closure is an equivalence on (chart vertex, component) slots and merging those columns is that block's exact Gauss-Jordan. Non-node slots of a class copy the class's exact value; a class reaching no node takes its mean snapped to F_d (MC19 5.3.1 steps 2-3). The merge also SHRINKS the BigInteger system instead of growing it: fandisk 85 cut branches + 655 alignment rows over 170 node sectors come to 286 columns, bolt 46 + 101 over 92 to 175, so the IRREF stays milliseconds. The 5.4 unflip repair now also refuses to move a vertex with an incident align edge. Also fixed ParameterizationMetrics.measureAlignmentResidual to bound its loop by alignmentEdgeIsoAxis.length (active edges) rather than mesh.edgeCount().

FANDISK LOADS END TO END. Log: '[motorcycle] arrangement patches: 765 cycles, 765 valid rectangles, 0 unresolved', 'hop turns: ... lawViolations=0', 'Def 3.1 rectangularity: violations=0', arcsSharingANodePair=0 (the line no longer prints), '[embed] arcs=1586 copy V=11530 E=34584 F=23056', '[embed] dissolved 21 degree-two node(s)', '[quad-layout] global grid map 1.193s', '[quad-layout] patch surfaces 0.020s'. Three things got it there, all at trace time except the last. (1) The MC19 alignment rows: once a crease edge is bit-exactly iso, a separatrix that runs along a crease runs along MESH EDGES, so it leaves each face at a corner. cornerExits on fandisk go 22 -> 616 and that is the correct regime, not a bug (MC19 section 6 lists 'tracing along a sequence of aligned edges' as one of the things exact constraints make well defined). (2) EGKT08 section 5's rule keyed on the VERTEX, not on a chord: MotorcycleGraph.meetTrailsThroughVertex records every mesh vertex a trace drives through and pairs a new arrival with the trails already there. A per-face chord index structurally cannot see this case, because the two traces running along one crease record their segments in the two different faces that flank it. The direction test is exact and axis-based: ChartWalker.transportAroundVertex walks the vertex fan with crossEdge so the stored trail's axis and sign are read in the arriving trace's chart, composing the cut transitions in between; same axis means driving onto the track (crash), perpendicular means a valence-4 crossing and both arcs are split there. (3) crashOntoTrail keeps EGKT08's oppositely-travelling clause, so a head-on pair stops together.

The one new piece downstream of the tracer: a head-on pair stopping together leaves a degree-TWO T-mesh node at the contact, which is a shape this pipeline had never produced (on master traces drive through each other, so it never arose) and which LayoutResolution.requireSingleArcSides rejects with 'a degree-two node interior to a side has to be merged away first'. On fandisk there were exactly 21, one per head-on pair, confirmed 1:1 by a [motorcycle-diag] degree-2 dump. ArcNetwork.dissolveDegreeTwoNodes now merges the two arcs at such a node into one and retires the node: it runs after assemble(), where the carve has already produced both arcs' copy-edge paths, so the merge is a concatenation of two ArcEdgePaths plus a re-claim and the removal of the retired arc and the node from the incident patches' sideArcIds/sideNodeIds. The kept arc never changes orientation (the retired one's path is reversed into place instead), so leftPatchId/rightPatchId and the patch walk order stay as assemble() set them. Two earlier attempts are recorded as dead ends: splicing the two traces' chains fails because SnappingCarve.sliceArc routes an arc through its OWN trace's segments and TraceSegment has no entry-edge index to reverse ('T-mesh node 813 has no barycentric in source face 3827'); and letting the arriving trace drive on over a retired partner's trail never terminates (the event backstop fires after 115632 events with 106 traces still queued), because a blanket exemption from crashing lets traces loop round closed iso curves.

None of this ticket's new trace-time rules fire on bolt (no vertex-trail meeting, no crash, no degree-two node), so the whole delta is the 101 now-exact alignment rows moving chart values in the last ulps and with them where two separatrices cross.

FINDING ONLY, no change made: MotorcycleGraph.orient2d is (bx-ax)*(cy-ay) - (by-ay)*(cx-ax) in plain doubles, and QuadLayoutPsuedoCode.md section E prescribes QEx-style exact predicates ('Use exact predicates (QEx Algorithm 1 ...)'). The projector's F_d outputs do NOT make that determinant exact by construction. An F_d value is an integer multiple of 2^(K-52) with magnitude below d = 2^K, so a difference of two of them is exact only while the difference itself stays below d (it is then a 53-bit multiple of the same quantum); the two PRODUCTS are each up to about 106 significant bits and round, and the subtraction that follows can then cancel catastrophically. So the general three-point form is inexact at any scale. Two of orient2d's three uses are exact anyway and not by luck: in spawnFromSingularities the third point is a corner plus a unit axis direction, so orient2d(au,av,bu,bv,au+dir0,av+dir1) reduces to (bu-au)*dir1 - (bv-av)*dir0 with dir in {0,+-1} - one product is zero and the other is a sign flip - and orient2d(0,0,edgeU,edgeV,dir0,dir1) reduces the same way. The one genuinely inexact call is the chart-triangle orientation test orient2d(au,av,bu,bv,cu,cv) that gates port spawning, and SeamlessProjector.orient2dHelper has the same shape in the section 5.4 flip test and the kernel clip. Both are sign tests on non-degenerate triangles (flippedTriangleCount is 0 on all five meshes), so they are reliable in practice but not guaranteed; making them exact needs a Shewchuk-style adaptive orient2d, which is a separate ticket.

On sync, keep 117's in-flight head-on scan (this diff has no equivalent and two traces crossing one face concurrently are still invisible to FaceSegmentIndex here) and drop its 1e-9 tolerance: this diff restored the bit-exact iso test and, with the alignment rows in the projector, fandisk's same-axis gap is now 0 ulps (worstLevelGap=0.00, collinearMeetings=0) where it was 64 ulps. 117's 1361 same-axis pairs on bolt at bias -0.5 with a worst gap of 2.27e-13 must be re-measured after this change before any tolerance is reinstated; if a gap survives it is not alignment residual and needs its own explanation. The two diffs' crash rules are complementary, not duplicates: 117's fires on chords inside one face, this one's on a mesh VERTEX two traces drive through from different faces, which no per-face chord index can see.
